2026-11:
Forecaster's note (Claude, 17 October 2026, re-issued with GEFS). November begins under one of the strongest El Niños in the record: over 8 September–7 October relative Niño-3.4 was at the 98th percentile of that window since 1959 (+2.6 °C on the RONI scale; Niño-3.4 itself +3.3 °C), and the closest analogue years are 2015, 1982, 1997 and 2023. This issue adds GEFS's forecast of 1–15 November from the 15 October run. Both point to a warm month: the statistical forecast is warmest over the Barents and Kara Seas, central Europe and Alaska, and GEFS puts its largest first-half anomalies over Siberia (+3 to +4 °C), the Kara Sea and Alaska. The blend keeps above normal favoured over most of the hemisphere, most strongly over central Europe (about 70 %), the Aleutians and the Arctic (about 60 %). On the 2000–2019 reforecast years, adding GEFS raised November's temperature correlation from +0.15 to +0.22.

Where they disagree: GEFS has a ridge over the North Pacific and the Aleutians in the first half and a deep low over the pole, while in the six strongest El Niño Novembers since 1959 the Aleutian low deepened in five (by about 27 m) and Siberia was colder than its trend in all six. The blend gives GEFS a weight of only about 0.1 for 500 hPa height, because its first-half height pattern has said little about the November mean (hindcast ACC +0.10), so the height map stays close to the statistical forecast and remains the least reliable part. Siberia is where the blend moved most: the statistical forecast had it near normal, GEFS is very warm for the first half, and the blend sits near +1 °C, with probabilities close to equal chances. The precipitation map still carries the El Niño wet signal along the Gulf Coast and the southeastern United States (about +0.6 mm/day), but November precipitation skill is significant over only 3 % of the hemisphere: a lean, not a call.
